Kids Clubs

Best Resorts With Kids Clubs

By Marcus Webb · May 28, 2026 · Updated August 26, 2026 · 8 min read

A great kids’ club can change the entire tone of a family vacation — kids who are genuinely having fun instead of just supervised, and parents who get real, guilt-free time to themselves. This roundup focuses specifically on resorts that get that program right, not just resorts that happen to have a room labeled “kids’ club.”

Quick facts

Typical age range
3–12 years, with separate teen programs at some resorts
What to ask about
Staff-to-child ratio and daily activity schedule

Not all kids' clubs are the same

'Kids' club' can mean anything from a genuinely engaging, staffed program with a real daily schedule to a room with some toys and minimal supervision. The difference matters — a good kids' club is often what makes a parents' vacation feel like an actual vacation, not just parenting somewhere warmer.

What separates a great kids' club from an average one

A real, published daily schedule

The best kids' clubs post an actual itinerary — crafts, pool time, a scavenger hunt — rather than open-ended free play. Ask to see a sample schedule before booking if it's not published online.

Coral Lagoon Resort & Spa, Riviera Maya

Staff who stay genuinely engaged with kids rather than just supervising from the sidelines, plus an in-room crib and baby-monitor rental option for younger siblings. See our full review.

Age-segmented groups

The strongest programs split kids into meaningful age bands — a 4-year-old and a 10-year-old have very different needs, and a resort that group them together for lack of capacity usually shows it.

Evening and teen programming

A smaller number of resorts extend supervised activities into the evening or offer a genuine teen lounge, which can be the deciding factor for families with a wider age range of kids.

Questions to ask before you book

  • What's the staff-to-child ratio, and is it consistent throughout the day or reduced during off-peak hours?
  • Is the kids' club included in the room rate or a separate daily charge?
  • What's the minimum age, and is it strictly enforced?
  • Can you drop in and observe a session before committing to leave your child there for a full day?

Getting the most out of a good kids' club

  • Bring a labeled water bottle and a spare change of clothes on drop-off days — most clubs ask for this and it's easy to forget on day one
  • Introduce your child to the space with you present for the first short session, rather than a full-day drop-off immediately
  • Use the club deliberately for at least one longer adult block — it's part of what a family resort's rate is paying for

Frequently asked questions

What age can kids usually start at a resort kids' club?

Most resorts set the minimum between 3 and 5 years old, and some still require full toilet training. Always confirm directly, as policies vary significantly by property.

Is a resort's kids' club included in the room price?

It depends on the resort — many all-inclusive properties include it, while others charge a separate daily or hourly fee. Confirm this before booking if it factors into your budget.

How do you know if a kids' club is actually good before you arrive?

Ask the resort directly for a sample daily schedule and staff-to-child ratio, and look for recent parent reviews that mention the kids' club specifically rather than the resort in general.
